title: Geometric representations of permutations
key_idea: Permutations have beautiful geometric representations: permutation matrices, diagrams, and increasing binary trees. Pattern-avoiding permutations (132-avoiding, 321-avoiding) are counted by the Catalan numbers $C_n = \frac{1}{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}$. Increasing binary trees encode Eulerian statistics.
summary: The diagram $D_w$ of a permutation captures its inversions geometrically. 321-avoiding permutations (no decreasing subsequence of length 3) biject with certain lattice paths, and 132-avoiding permutations biject with Young diagrams fitting in a staircase — both sets have Catalan number size. Increasing binary trees encode permutations bijectively, with the number of left children giving the Eulerian number count.

notation.description: Diagram of $w$: cells $(i,j)$ with $i < w^{-1}(j)$ and $j < w(i)$

definitions.statement: The **diagram** of $w \in \mathfrak{S}_n$ is $$D_w = \{(i,j) \in [n]\times[n] : w(i) \neq j,\, w^{-1}(j) \neq i,\, i < w^{-1}(j),\, j < w(i)\}.$$ Equivalently, $(i,j) \in D_w$ iff column $j$ is to the left of the $1$ in row $i$ of $P_w$, and row $i$ is above the $1$ in column $j$.

For $w = w_1 \cdots w_n \in \mathfrak{S}_n$, the **increasing binary tree** $T(w)$ is defined recursively: find the position $i$ where $w_i = $ minimum of $w$; then $i$ is the root, $T(u)$ (left subtree) is built from $w_1\cdots w_{i-1}$, and $T(v)$ (right subtree) from $w_{i+1}\cdots w_n$. The tree is **increasing** because each parent label is less than its children's labels.

The **unordered increasing tree** $T'(w)$: vertex $i$ is a child of the rightmost $j < i$ that appears to the left of $i$ in $w$ (if no such $j$, $i$ is a child of the root $0$).

propositions.title: 132-avoiding permutations and partitions
propositions.statement:
There is a bijection between 132-avoiding permutations in $\mathfrak{S}_n$ and partitions $\lambda = (\lambda_1 \geq \cdots \geq \lambda_n \geq 0)$ with $\lambda_i \leq n-i$ (partitions fitting in the staircase $(n-1, n-2, \ldots, 0)$). Moreover, under this bijection, $\text{inv}(w) = |\lambda|$, so $$\sum_{w \in \mathcal{S}_{132}(n)} q^{\text{inv}(w)} = \sum_{\lambda} q^{|\lambda|}$$
where $\lambda$ ranges over partitions fitting in the staircase.

propositions.title: Increasing binary trees and Eulerian numbers
propositions.statement:
(a) The number of increasing binary trees on vertex set $[n]$ is $n!$.
(b) The number of such trees with exactly $k$ left successors (vertices with a left child) is the Eulerian number $A(n, k+1)$.
(c) The number of **complete** increasing binary trees on $2n+1$ vertices is the Euler number $E_{2n+1}$.
propositions.proof_sketch: The bijection $w \mapsto T(w)$ is a bijection $\mathfrak{S}_n \to$ (increasing binary trees on $[n]$). A left successor in $T(w)$ corresponds to a descent in $w$, establishing (b). For complete trees (every vertex has 0 or 2 children), alternating permutations are in bijection with such trees.

propositions.title: Unordered increasing trees and Stirling/Euler numbers
propositions.statement:
For unordered increasing trees $T'(w)$ on vertex set $\{0,1,\ldots,n\}$ (root labeled $0$):
(a) The number of such trees is $n!$.
(b) The number with exactly $k$ children of the root equals $c(n,k)$ (signless Stirling number of the first kind).
(c) The number with exactly $k$ leaves (vertices with no children) equals the Eulerian number $A(n,k)$.

examples.title: Catalan numbers from 321-avoiding permutations
examples.solution: 321-avoiding permutations biject with ballot sequences (lattice paths from $(0,0)$ to $(n,n)$ not going below the diagonal): map $w$ to the path that goes right when reading $w$ from right to left (if current value is larger than any future value, go up; else right). The count of such paths is $C_n$.

exercises.statement: Show that the number of 132-avoiding permutations in $\mathfrak{S}_n$ is the Catalan number $C_n = \frac{1}{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}$.
hints: Use the bijection with staircase partitions: $|\mathcal{S}_{132}(n)|$ = # partitions inside the staircase $(n-1,n-2,\ldots,1,0)$. This is a well-known Catalan number identity.

text_passages.text: The permutation matrix $P_w$ has a $1$ in position $(i, w(i))$ for each $i$. The **diagram** $D_w$ captures inversions geometrically: $(i,j) \in D_w$ if cell $(i,j)$ is strictly to the right of the $1$ in column $j$ and strictly above the $1$ in row $i$.

text_passages.label: Definition — Permutation diagram
text_passages.preview: $D_w = \{(i,j): i < w^{-1}(j)$ and $j < w(i)\}$. This cell set encodes inversions and pattern structure.

text_passages.text: A permutation $w$ is **321-avoiding** if it has no decreasing subsequence of length 3. Similarly, $w$ is **132-avoiding** if there are no $i < j < k$ with $w_k < w_i < w_j$. Both sets have Catalan number size $C_n = \frac{1}{n+1}\binom{2n}{n}$.

text_passages.label: Proposition 1.5.1 — 132-avoiding and partitions
text_passages.preview: $\sum_{w \in \mathcal{S}_{132}(n)} q^{\text{inv}(w)} = \sum_{\lambda} q^{|\lambda|}$ where $\lambda$ ranges over partitions in the staircase $(n-1,\ldots,0)$. Setting $q=1$ gives $|\mathcal{S}_{132}(n)| = C_n$.

text_passages.label: Definition — Increasing binary tree
text_passages.preview: $T(w)$ is built recursively: the position of the minimum is the root, left subtree from elements before it, right subtree from elements after. The bijection $w \leftrightarrow T(w)$ links tree structure to permutation statistics.

text_passages.label: Proposition 1.5.3 — Trees and Eulerian numbers
text_passages.preview: (a) Increasing binary trees on $[n]$: $n!$ total. (b) Trees with $k$ left successors: $A(n,k+1)$ (Eulerian number). (c) Complete trees on $2n+1$ vertices: $E_{2n+1}$ (Euler number).

text_passages.label: Proposition 1.5.5 — Unordered increasing trees
text_passages.preview: Unordered increasing trees on $\{0,\ldots,n\}$: (a) $n!$ total; (b) $k$ children of root $\leftrightarrow c(n,k)$ (Stirling 1st kind); (c) $k$ leaves $\leftrightarrow A(n,k)$ (Eulerian).
